title: Financial toxicity among adults receiving systemic cancer treatment at a regional cancer centre
subtitle: Cross-sectional survey to inform screening and a financial navigation service
statement: Clinicians at a regional cancer centre see patients who delay treatment or miss appointments because of costs, but the centre does not know how common financial toxicity is among the 1,900 adults starting systemic treatment each year, who is most affected, or whether the financial problems checkbox in its distress screening finds them. A cross-sectional survey with a validated questionnaire can estimate prevalence by group and inform a decision on a financial navigation service.
whoAffected: Adults receiving systemic cancer treatment and their families, especially younger patients, those on low incomes, those who stopped working and those living far from the centre; supportive care staff; centre leadership deciding on navigation.
whatHurts: Costs of travel, parking, medicines and lost income can push patients to delay or skip treatment and cause lasting hardship for families; unmet need is invisible if screening misses it.
currentPractice: Distress screening at the first treatment visit with a financial problems checkbox; referral to social work at clinician discretion; no measurement of financial toxicity.
whyNow: Ethics approval is in place, interpreter funding is available, and leadership wants evidence before deciding on a navigation service.
constraints: Coordinator two days a week; three months of recruitment; four languages; no linkage to billing or benefit records.
patientCenteredGoal: No patient delays or abandons cancer treatment because of its costs, and those at risk are found early and helped.
summary: Problem framed as a cross-sectional survey of financial toxicity with screening agreement as a second question.
